It takes a lot of courage to share what you are going through. Dealing with a binge-exercise cycle since you were a teenager sounds incredibly exhausting, and it is completely understandable that you feel overwhelmed by shame and disappointment. Please know that you are not alone in this, and these behaviors are often just your mind's way of trying to cope with intense stress. 

To help break this cycle, try practicing self-compassion instead of punishment after a binge. Remind yourself that one moment does not define you, and try to gently redirect your focus to a calming activity rather than immediately heading to the gym. Learning to identify your specific stress triggers and finding alternative ways to soothe your nervous system—like deep breathing, taking a gentle walk, or journaling—can also be powerful. Because this has been a long-standing pattern, reaching out to a therapist who specializes in disordered eating could provide you with the personalized tools and support you deserve to fully heal your relationship with food.
